newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish shares rebound, seen up on Thursday.
newsitem.headline: Polish shares rebound, seen up on Thursday.

text.p: Polish shares rebounded sharply on Wednesday after a 10-session fall and analysts said that though the market should rise again on Thursday, a return to a significant growth trend did not seem likely.
"We should have more growth tomorrow, though not as much as today, and then consolidation," said Jacek Radziwonka, a trader at Bank Staropolski brokerage.

Analysts said investors had been taking profits after the market's 100-percent surge this year, with the current market's mood soured by parliament's lower house's surprise decision last week to cut taxes for low earners, seen as inflationary.

The main market's all-share WIG index rose 3.2 percent to 13,280.2 and turnover fell 7.6 percent 89.4 million zlotys ($31.8 million) on both markets. Gainers led losers by 72 to five with three stocks flat.
Analysts said top gainer food trader and producer Animex, up 9.8 percent in active trade, was helped by a newspaper report it would continue to try to receive interest from overpaid tax.
Analysts were surprised by the scale of bank WBK's 9.4-percent jump despite its recent 18.8-percent fall.
Biggest loser construction firm Espebepe fell 10 percent, continuing to drop after its president said last week the firm was threatened with bankruptcy, analysts said.
Continuous trade turnover was at 2.9 million zlotys ($1 million) with biggest mover Animex up 7.9 percent.

Mass privatisation NFI units rose six percent to 140.5 million zlotys ($50) in the regular bourse session and rose 4.7 percent to 145 zlotys ($51.6) in continuous trade, with stronger post-price-fixing buying at the main session signalling another rise on Thursday, analysts said.
